nodes.name: Write Summary
nodes.notes: Only writes when the text actually changed, so a sweep over an unchanged event costs nothing.

nodes.name: IF Staffing Just Completed?
nodes.notes: Only on the call that writes the complete summary, and only when that write succeeded. The written summary is the marker that the email has gone, so a later call (from 40 or the 50 sweep) sees it and stays quiet. If the write failed nothing is sent, and the next call retries.

nodes.name: Compose Completion Email
nodes.notes: The publish link contains Administrate merge fields in double braces. Those cannot appear inside an n8n expression, because n8n tries to evaluate them as its own and fails with invalid syntax. Building the string here keeps the braces out of any node parameter.

nodes.name: Auto Publish If Enabled
nodes.notes: Runs a harmless no-op query unless the event is set to publish automatically and the required personnel are genuinely met.

nodes.name: Save Publish Link
nodes.notes: One publish token per event. Saving a new one expires the link in any earlier completion email.

nodes.notes: The same news as the coordinator gets, minus the publish link, because only the coordinator can act on it. parameters.content:
## 20 Recompute Event Summary (shared)

Called by **40 Response Handler** after a response and by **50 Reminders and Expiry** after a reminder and on its daily refresh. It is the only place the staffing summary is calculated and the only place the staffing complete email is sent, so the wording, the completeness rule and the email cannot drift between callers.

### What it does
1. Works out the summary and writes it to the event when the text changed.
2. When staffing has *just* become complete and that write succeeded, it publishes automatically if **Publish Automatically** is Yes. Unless **Suppress Completion Email** is Yes, it saves a fresh publish token (replacing the event's old one) and emails the coordinator a link to **60**.

### One email per completion
The summary stored on the event is the marker. Once the complete summary is written, every later call from 40 or 50 sees it and sends nothing. If the write fails, nothing is sent and the next call (at the latest the next daily sweep) tries again. A coordinator added after completion is picked up the same way.

### Rules worth knowing
- A required coordinator is shown in the breakdown but not counted, because a coordinator never answers an invitation.
- *Needs attention* only shows while the event is a draft and still short.

### Setup
Administrate OAuth2 credential on every HTTP Request node. Activate is not needed: it runs when called. Copy this workflow's ID into `SUMMARY_WORKFLOW_ID` in 40 and 50.

## Config

**COORDINATOR_ROLE_NAME** - the staff role that coordinates the event. Excluded from the counts and used to address the completion email. Must match the role name in Administrate.

**INVITATIONS_TABLE_ID** - the invitations Data Table.

**PUBLISH_LINKS_TABLE_ID** - the publish links Data Table. One token per event.

**PUBLISH_PAGE_URL** - production URL of **60 Publish Event Page**.

**SUMMARY_FIELD_KEY** - `definitionKey` of the Event text field that shows the summary.

**AUTO_PUBLISH_FIELD_KEY**, **SUPPRESS_EMAIL_FIELD_KEY** - Event Yes/No field keys for automatic publishing and for stopping the completion email.

**CHECKBOX_TRUE_VALUES** - values that count as yes. Anything else means no.

**PUBLISHED_STATE** - lifecycle state used when publishing automatically.

**COMPLETE_PREFIX** - text a complete summary starts with. It is also the marker that the completion email has gone, so changing it makes every event look newly complete once.

**ORIGIN_IDENTIFIER**, **SENDING_ADDRESS_ID**, **VERB_BASE**, **VERB_GERUND**, **BRAND_NAME**, **EMAIL_PALETTE**, **EMAIL_SHELL**, **EMAIL_BUTTON** - as in 40 and 50.
